activeMilestone.exitCondition: All scenarios complete through endings with readable rendering, responsive choices, sustained audio, save/load resume, and measured long-run stability without unsupported stops

lastCompletedBoundary.summary: Release Chrome resumed the validated save and returned to the exact title target after 174.85 seconds with 135 Presents, 10 completed pointer actions, and 5 audio playbacks; no unsupported endpoint, WebGL error, pending host work, lease leak, or source mutation was observed, and the persisted 95,058-byte save remained hash-identical

currentForwardStop.reason: The release forward run returned to the exact title target and stopped with outcome checkpoint-complete after 135 Presents; the final frame independently matched the bounded title color and dark-region probes, while source immutability, zero pending host work, an inactive profile lease, and unchanged save bytes were preserved

nextDevelopmentGoal: Build on the verified counted-loop and checked SIMD-window compiler, reduce remaining CPU-heavy frame work and input/transition latency in actual Chrome play while retaining v86 fallback, then resume additional routes and long-run acceptance

supportedSubsystems.summary: PE32 loading, JIT-enabled x86 execution and the performance island share one Rust-owned GuestMemory arena with checked mapping and write receipts; process/thread scheduling, callbacks and generic forward capture remain active, while normal/debug v86 retain the separate copying mirror and differential oracle

Logical window, message queue, timers, focus/cursor state, keyboard scan, primary down/up dispatch, and native double-click generation are active; the validated save/load continuation accepted input through the first route ending and exact title return

GDI/GDI+ reached paths and bounded D3D9 fixed-function scenes publish through WebGL2; the ending run produced 135 Presents and returned to the exact title color and dark-region signature with WebGL error zero

Immutable source reads and a title-local SQLite overlay remain separated; the latest 95,058-byte Q.Save stayed hash-identical through the ending run with the lease inactive afterward, while the executable and source assets remained unchanged

Reached DirectSound streaming buffers support concurrent non-overlapping partial and wrapping Lock/Unlock, captured notification waits, cursor/status/control, and Play/Stop through generation-safe Chrome Web Audio transport; five non-zero playbacks occurred in the ending run and sustained audio spans the accepted route

importantNonClaims: Only the first default route ending is accepted; alternate choices, alternate routes, all-scenario completion, and long-run acceptance are not yet claimed

The accepted checkpoint is .work-only and retains one 95,058-byte Q.Save with SHA-256 0cd7c853e9c4afd032e9f1235c2a9bb065d6b5a15cb35fc57c87921a991306ec; the ending run hydrated it unchanged and did not overwrite it
The measured route live set is bounded to 480 MiB; later-route peak memory and long-run reclamation are not yet accepted
Primary audio spans the representative flow, but format breadth, suspend/resume behavior, and long-run streaming stability are not yet accepted

Performance mode retains JIT across data mapping changes, selectively rearms dirty-page TLB entries, and delivers independent live host completions without historical replay serialization (two measured transitions improved from 4.42s/3.33s to 1.60s/0.54s). Fused x87 memory operations, exact binary32 widening, guarded native 53-bit arithmetic and batched memory-journal allocation further reduced a CPU-heavy transition from 3.76-4.11s to 2.70-2.83s in Chrome (two runs per variant). Startup through 12 inputs improved from 52.17-53.30s to 50.10-50.26s at 279-287M guest instructions/sec, with zero observed audio underruns but 83ms maximum slices. Independent normal-engine differential checks cover rounding, precision, special values and exponent boundaries; memory rollback retains original bytes and ordering. The normal/debug v86 artifact is unchanged. Whole-run Presents/sec is not steady-play FPS, and 60 FPS-class response remains unaccepted

The direct-memory performance island removes CPU/GuestMemory page copies while preserving Rust frame ownership, zero-initialization, checked protection and transactional rollback. Chrome 152.0.7977.83 startup/12-input runs used 539MB of Wasm memory versus 660MB with the previous MMX island; measured TS writeback synchronization fell from 1.11-1.18s to about 64ms, but wall time remained 50.4-51.7s and maximum slices reached 70-116ms across startup/load checks. Normal/debug keep their unchanged artifact and diagnostic heap fills. These results establish memory/copy reduction, not 60 FPS or a broad speedup

Binary host deltas now stream authoritative frames without intermediate page allocations/copies; randomized normal/direct-memory checks preserve exact wire bytes, generations and rollback. Isolated 20-input Chrome load continuations preserve the accepted 95,058-byte save, immutable source, inactive lease and nonblack final frame with zero pending work. Maximum slices fell from 153-201ms to 69-80ms and Wasm memory from 579MB to 556MB; sampled delta generation fell from 1.205s to 0.711s. Removing unconsumed diagnostic hashes and repeated full large-page scans further reduced sampled page-fault service from 1.179s to 0.245s; insertion-time range/alignment validation, release endpoint checks and full debug audits remain. Whole-run time remains about 144s, with two underruns and an 85ms maximum slice in the latest load run. A 393s trusted mouse/keyboard check produced 2,773 draw notifications, nonzero audio, zero underruns/pending calls and full cleanup of seven audio nodes. Enter/left-click next-draw waits still reached 3.83s/0.90s; the latter entered Rust in 20ms and its window callback completed in 36ms. Static-title intervals and next-draw timings do not prove semantic latency. Normal/debug CPU artifacts and the wire contract are unchanged; overall speedup, playable load, sustained 60 FPS response and long-run acceptance remain unclaimed

The v47 Chrome run fixes an audio lifetime race at its shared owners: DirectSound Stop persists a consumable Rust Event signal, WaitForSingleObject supports zero/infinite Thread waits, and the browser bridge acknowledges committed Rust wakeups. The old audio threads now exit before handle/buffer reuse. A matched 30-second profiled playback window supplied 33.3s of audio with zero underruns, versus 11 updates and 126 underruns in the preceding MMX-only run. A separate 162s trusted mouse/Enter manual run continued drawing and multiple nonzero WebAudio spans with zero underruns, but next-canvas-frame delays of 63ms, 2.07s and 4.52s still reject sustained responsiveness. Generic MMX arithmetic lowering reduced a 40.9M-instruction synthetic median from 288ms to 251ms; whole-game speedup is not established (87.49s profiled run, 251M instructions/sec, maximum slice 144ms). Normal/debug CPU artifacts remain unchanged; Windows thread/event fixes are shared

The bounded counted-loop compiler reuses v86 decoding, cache invalidation and precise fallback but lowers proven integer/MMX loops without per-instruction memory-state round trips. A 65,536-pixel kernel in ordinary RAM improved from 2.68-2.72ms to 0.18-0.20ms with matching output and instruction count. The earlier test overlapping VGA-reserved memory is not a RAM benchmark. Profiled Chrome playback tail windows improved median draw intervals from 59-69ms to 33-44ms across candidates; these timer-driven windows are not identical frame workloads. The shipped counted-loop candidate's 147s trusted mouse/Escape/Enter run produced 2,454 Presents and nonzero audio with no unsupported endpoint or pending host calls. Next changed-frame delays were 23-39ms for two left clicks but 2.3-3.9s for right-click/keyboard, with a 77ms maximum slice. One profiled integer-extension run observed one audio underrun; sustained responsiveness and 60 FPS remain unaccepted. Normal/debug artifact hashes are unchanged

Direct mapping reuse removes redundant protection-only page recreation (profiled tail mapping cost about 1.10s to 8ms); ordered free-frame reuse reduces fragmented render copies (readGuestBytes 769-790ms to 39-61ms). Counted-loop side entries now return at exhausted JIT budgets instead of stranding remaining iterations on the slow path; the focused regression fails on the previous engine. Two Chrome runs measured 354-357M guest instructions/sec and tail draw medians 26.9-27.9ms versus the previous 28.8-40.2ms, with 81-85ms maximum slices and one/zero audio underruns. Timer-driven workloads differ, so the magnitude is not a matched FPS gain. A 208s trusted IAB run produced nonzero audio, zero underruns and no pending host work; right-click/Escape/Enter next-changed-canvas delays were 31/37/476ms and maximum slice 70ms. Input phases differ from earlier manual checks and do not establish transition speedup. All six audio nodes disconnected and closed on Stop. Sustained 60 FPS-class response and new save/load acceptance remain unclaimed; normal/debug CPU artifacts are unchanged

Checked SIMD windows reuse the existing JIT and fallback while keeping XMM/MMX intermediates in Wasm locals; resident ordinary-RAM, mapping, protection, alignment, control-state and alias guards preserve the original fault path. Independent numeric regressions pass on the candidate, v84 and unchanged normal/debug artifacts, including mid-block windows, exact normal budgets, dirty rearm, remap, code writes and faults. Two profiled Chrome runs measured 361-363M guest instructions/sec versus 343-346M for interleaved v84 controls. One near-matched heavy frame improved from 751ms/247.64M instructions to 662ms/247.05M (about 12% shorter); tail draw medians remain 27-28ms, and timer-driven workloads do not establish a matched overall FPS gain. A 216s trusted mouse/keyboard run produced 2,699 draw notifications, nonzero WebAudio and zero underruns or pending host calls; Enter/Escape next-draw delays were still 825/228ms and maximum slice 83ms. Draw notification timing is not changed-frame or semantic-completion latency. All six audio nodes disconnected and closed on Stop. Sustained 60 FPS-class response, exact NaN payloads, exact fault-retirement counts and new save/load acceptance remain unclaimed

Single-protection direct-memory updates now preflight existing mappings without rebuilding an allocation plan, and rare dirty-overflow/restoration scans reuse the page map instead of maintaining a second writable-page index. Sampled mapping cost fell from 1.69s to 1.02-1.05s per 30s tail; two Chrome runs measured 370-372M guest instructions/sec and 24.8-25.3ms median draw intervals with zero audio underruns. Timer-driven workloads differ, so these are not matched FPS gains. A 411s trusted mouse/keyboard check produced 3,430 draw notifications, nonzero audio, zero underruns/pending host calls and complete audio cleanup on Stop, but Enter/right-click next-draw delays reached 2.85s/1.19s. The 16.69ms browser rAF median is not guest FPS; sustained responsiveness remains unaccepted. Late-page protection failure and dirty restoration regressions pass; normal/debug CPU artifacts are unchanged

Counted loops now defer checks for streams used only inside the first conditional MMX branch until that branch is entered; skipped iterations need no mapping, and a failed guard rolls back only the write-free current prefix before ordinary-JIT fallback. Numeric regressions cover unused unmapped/readonly streams, late actual faults and exact normal budgets. Two Chrome candidates measured 379-383M instructions/sec; the complete repeat's 24.45ms median draw interval compares with 26.41ms/368M instructions/sec in an interleaved control, but timer-driven workloads differ and no matched overall FPS gain is claimed. A 189s trusted mouse/keyboard run produced 2,976 draw notifications, nonzero audio, zero underruns/pending host work and full audio cleanup; maximum slice was 62ms. Start/left/Enter/right/Escape next-draw delays were 22/6/9/47/319ms, not semantic-completion latency. The first click on a static title waited until the later Start action, demonstrating why no-draw intervals alone do not measure input lag. Normal/debug artifacts remain unchanged; sustained 60 FPS response, new save/load and long-run acceptance remain unclaimed
